title: Design: A/R Summary opening screen matches the design picture
custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as a user with the "Admin" role, with {Location-A} as your current location.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • The organization has open documents in these reports at two locations, {Location-A} and {Location-B}, and you are enrolled at both; {Location-A}'s name comes first in A to Z order.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 and {Location-B} is Staging Lethbridge - 4310.
  • The report lists customers at both locations on today's date, including at least one with a credit balance (a negative Total) and one with a long name.
    For example: the QA organization's A/R Summary (46 customers).
  • Starting screen: A/R Summary (Reports, then "A/R Aging Summary" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu) is open in a desktop browser window 1440 px wide, as opened from the Reports menu in light theme at 100% zoom.
  • The design picture "A/R Aging Summary opens A to Z" (ar-ap-p1-a-r-aging-summary-opens-a-to-z.png) is attached to this case and open beside the browser at 100% zoom; compare the layout, labels and styles, not the names and amounts, which are only examples.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Compare the title row with the picture.
  2. Compare the filter row with the picture, chip by chip.
  3. Compare the column headings with the picture, left to right, letter for letter.
  4. Compare the customer name cells and the money cells with the picture.
  5. Scroll the table down a little and look at the Totals row.
  6. Look at how the table sits on the page.
  7. Widen the browser window to 1536 px and look across the page.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the title "A/R Aging Summary", a grey circled "i" info icon directly right of it, and a grey "⋯" button at the far right, all on one line, as in the picture.
  • Step 2: four chips in this order: "As of: " and the date in a blue pill with a calendar icon and a down arrow; "Customer: All customers" with a person icon and no fill (resting); "Past due: Any" with an hourglass icon and no fill (resting); "Location: All locations" with a location pin icon in a blue pill.
  • Step 3: "Customer" with a small up arrow (the sorted column), "Location", "Current", "1-30 Days", "31-60 Days", "61-90 Days", "91 And Over", "Total", in bold, each on one line; only "Customer" carries an arrow.
  • Step 4: customer names are blue and in A to Z order, a name starting "10" before one starting "2"; money is right-aligned, an empty bucket is blank, a credit shows the minus after the dollar sign (for example "$-100.00"), as today, and the Total column is bold on every row.
  • Step 5: the bold Totals row stays at the bottom of the table while the rows scroll under it, as in the picture.
  • Step 6: the table runs across the page with no card or frame around it, rows divided by thin lines, as in the picture.
  • Step 7: nothing overlaps, is cut off or clipped; the layout is the same as at 1440 px.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 5 (21 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 22 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11531 (Story 1, Reports open in QuickBooks name order), story SV-11535 (Story 5, Filters: customer or vendor, past due and location), story SV-11536 (Story 6, Location column), story SV-11538 (Story 8, Report descriptions and layout)

  • S8-R2: “The title, its info icon and the Export menu stay on one line at 1440 pixels wide; the filter row sits below them, positioned as on the native reports.”
  • S5-R1: “Each report's filter row is the native report filter row of the newer reports (Inventory Value, Sales By Customer), in this order on all six reports: the date chip ("As of: 10/15/2026"), the customer chip on the A/R reports or the vendor chip on the A/P reports, the Past due chip, then the Location chip.”
  • S5-R13: “The customer chip (A/R) and vendor chip (A/P) and their open menus are the native ones: Customer exactly as Sales By Customer's Customer filter (person icon), Vendor exactly as Inventory Value's Vendor filter (truck icon, "Search vendors"). The menu has a search box, an "All customers" or "All vendors" row, the native line "All customers are included. Pick one or more to narrow." (or vendors) while none is ticked, and the list; several can be ticked. The chip reads "Customer: All customers" or "Vendor: All vendors" in the resting (grey) style when none is ticked, the name when one is (shortened with "..." when long), and "Customer: N customers" or "Vendor: N vendors" when N are. The ticked customers or vendors narrow every row, group, total, page, sort and export; the Location list does not change (S5-R3).”
  • S5-R15: “The Past due chip and its open menu are the same native checkbox dropdown as Customer and Location: label "Past due", an hourglass icon, an "Any" row, the native line "All ranges are included. Pick one or more to narrow." while none is ticked, then "1-30 days", "31-60 days", "61-90 days", "91+ days", in that order; several can be ticked. The chip reads "Past due: Any" in the resting (grey) style when none is ticked, the range when one is (for example "Past due: 91+ days"), and "Past due: N ranges" when N are. Ticking all four reads "Past due: 4 ranges", not Any, because Any also keeps invoices and bills that are not due yet. The ranges are the reports' own aging buckets: 1 to 30, 31 to 60, 61 to 90 and more than 90 days past the due date on the as-of date.”
  • S1-R1: “A/R Summary opens with customers in name order, A to Z; A/P Summary opens with vendors in name order, A to Z.”
  • S1-R2: “Name order compares names ignoring capitals, in plain character order: digits and punctuation compare as characters, so "10 Trucking" comes before "2 Trucking" and "A-1 Towing" before "a1 towing".”
  • S1-R7: “The column the report opened on is marked as sorted: the name column on the Summaries and Detail reports, the Date column on Collection and Unpaid Invoices.”
  • S6-R3: “It sits right after the Date column, before the money columns; on A/R Summary and A/P Summary, which have no Date column, right after the customer or vendor name.”
  • S8-R3: “The headline column (Open Balance; Total on the Summaries) is pinned to the right edge and bold on the header, every row, every expanded row and the Totals row, as on Sales By Customer. At 1440 pixels wide every column of all six reports is visible without scrolling sideways: the customer or vendor name and Transaction type wrap long values onto a second line, Location wraps only on A/P Detail (nine columns), column headings never wrap, and money, date and number columns never wrap. Narrower than 1440 pixels, the table scrolls sideways under the pinned column.”
  • S8-R4: “The Totals row uses the native totals row style of the newer reports.”
  • What changes for existing users: “Which rows and amounts each user can see is unchanged: an untouched report shows exactly today's organization-wide numbers (apart from the Totals rows noted above), and the reports show money exactly as they do today.”
  • Key Decisions, reuse rule: “The reuse rule. Every control on these reports reuses an existing ShopView pattern: the native filter chips, the native totals row and pinned headline column of the newer reports, the existing location-switch prompt, the design system's chevron icon. Nothing new is drawn. Basis: d-reuse-existing-pattern.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

References from Design

Design canvas "A/R and A/P Report Sorting" (https://claude.ai/artifact/BRYCdjKwGRSgGPC9xxkgF4), read 22 Oct 2026: page 1 "Opening order and header sorting" (board Main.dc.html); page 7 "Filters and call list" (board Filters.dc.html). Compare the screen with the pictures below at 100% zoom; the expected results still come from the PRD quotes above, the pictures give the look and the on-screen labels.

Design pictures attached to this case:

  • ar-ap-p1-a-r-aging-summary-opens-a-to-z.png: figure "A/R Aging Summary opens A to Z" (This build (after)), board "1. Opening order and header sorting"
  • ar-ap-p7-four-chips-on-every-report.png: figure "Four chips on every report" (This build (after)), board "7. Filters and call list"
  • ar-ap-p7-a-r-summary-date-only.png: figure "A/R Summary: date only" (Production (before)), board "7. Filters and call list" (today's look, for comparison only)

The design's own words:

  • "Customer name order the way QuickBooks sorts ("10 Trucking" before "2 Trucking"), marked on the Customer header. S1-R1, S1-R2, S1-R4, S1-R7, S1-R8." (caption of "A/R Aging Summary opens A to Z")
  • "As of, Customer (Vendor on A/P), Past due, Location. "Customer: All customers" and "Past due: Any" rest grey, Past due with the design system’s hourglass icon. S5-R1, S5-R13, S5-R15." (caption of "Four chips on every report")
  • "The Summaries and Detail reports have no customer, vendor or past due filter today." (caption of "A/R Summary: date only")

Design note (DR-01): the design shows the Totals row sits on a light-grey band in some pictures (A/R Collection expanded, A/P Detail, A/P Unpaid Invoices, A/R Detail I32) and on the page colour in others (Summaries, I28, the same A/R Detail screen in I30). Closed without a question: PRD S8-R4: "The Totals row uses the native totals row style of the newer reports." The cases compare with Sales By Customer's Totals row; the pictures are not the reference for this one attribute.

Design note (DR-04): the design shows the Customer menu with two ticked shows the ticked names as tags in the search box, a clear "×", and "2 selected" on the "All customers" row. Closed without a question: No conflict: PRD S5-R13 "Customer exactly as Sales By Customer's Customer filter"; the PRD lists the menu's main rows, the design shows the native extras. The design case checks them.
